agents.name: manager
agents.system_message: A human manager. They will dictate the task and test finished drafts

agents.name: planner
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managers request. 
        Your job is the planner. When presented with a request, first try to understand what the manager is asking. Do this by explaining in more detail what the manager is asking for, and what the main challenges will be. Be specific and concise.

        Next, you should develop a plan to solve the request. Explain what will need to be done, and why, in the app. Have a logical order - this will be passed on to the programmer as a settled plan.

        Here is an example of what a settled plan would look like for a request:

        -----------

        The manager has asked us to {the managers request}.

        In other words, what the manager is asking for is {more complete request definition/explanation}

        This means, we need to {expand on functional requirements}


        A successful app for this task must achieve these things:
        1. Functionality/Feature 1
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 1 
        2. Functionality/Feature 2
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 2 
        3. Functionality/Feature 3
            - Guide for achieving Functionality/Feature 3 

        Do you agree, manager?

        ------------

        Nice and short and succicnt, while still having the necessary information. Please use this as a guide.

        Work with the manager until the manager approves of the plan. The manager will approve of the plan by using the phrase "sounds good"

        Once the manager said "sounds good", you can write a call to write_settled_plan to write the settled plan into memory. Do not alter the plan after manager approval. Simply remove the question, "Do you agree, manager?".

agents.name: programmer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the managerss request. Your job is the coder. You will be presented with a plan consisting of the necessary features and functional components. You will produce a python script which attempts to accomplish all of the tasks. However, some tasks are harder than others, and it may be best to leave a comment about what should be there, or what needs to be done. This is an iterative process, so you can expect a chance to revisit the code to fill in the blanks. You do not need to do everything on the first try. If you believe a section of code will be too hard to figure out on the first time, please consider leaving a note that can be tackled on the next iteration.
            
            Do not participate in any conversation or dialog. Your only output should be well formatted code blocks, and nothing else. It is someone elses job to review.
            
            You are only to produce code-blocks. Do not preempt the code with any extra text, and do not add any after it.

agents.name: reviewer
agents.system_message:
You and your group will be tasked with creating a python app which accomplishes the items set out in the plan. You are the reviewer. 
        You will review the managers request, the planners interpretation of the request, the approved plan, and the latest code iteration.

        Read through the code, and explain what you see in the code. Explain what look like it should work OK, as it relates to the request and plan.

        If there are errors, the code will go through another iteration. If you believe there are errors, to help guide the programmer, explain what is not OK, and why it is not OK.

        Do not write any code. Just explain in easy to understand terms.

        Your job is critical - please be logical, focus, and try your best.

requirements.description: Planner must produce a plan containing numbered functional requirements and wait for manager approval ('sounds good') before calling write_settled_plan.
expected_behavior: Planner outputs a plan with numbered functional requirements.
Planner asks manager for approval.
Manager says 'sounds good'.
Planner calls write_settled_plan to persist the plan.
negative_cases: Planner calls write_settled_plan without manager approval.
Planner alters plan after manager approval.

requirements.description: Coder must output only well-formatted code blocks, no extra text, and must not participate in conversation.
expected_behavior: Coder outputs only code blocks.
Coder does not add any text before or after code blocks.

requirements.description: Reviewer must evaluate code against the planoro produce a list of criticisms/comments without writing code.
expected_behavior: Reviewer explains what works and what does not.
Reviewer produces comments in easy-to-understand terms.
Reviewer does not write code.
negative_cases: Reviewer produces 100+ point list of the same issue.

requirements.description: Manager must be able to test code and provide feedback to Coder or Reviewer before exiting conversation.
expected_behavior: Manager can16 test script and provide feedback.
Coder or Reviewer updates output based on feedback.
Manager enters 'exit' to end conversation and trigger file write.
negative_cases: Encoding 'exit' does not trigger file write.
Encoding 'exit' does not move to next agent.

requirements.description: Iteration phase must present only the latest script and latest comments to Coder and Reviewer.
expected_behavior: Encoding Coder receives plan and latest script/comments.
Encoding Reviewer receives plan and latest script/comments.
Encoding version numbers increment correctly.
negative_cases: Encoding old script versions are presented.

requirements.description: Encoding write_latest_iteration must save code to script_v{n}.py and write_settled_plan must save plan to project folder.
expected_behavior: Encoding write_latest_iteration creates script_v{n}.py with correct version number.
Encoding write_settled_plan creates plan file in project folder.
negative_cases: Encoding write_settled_plan fails to create file.

requirements.description: Encoding program must support continuing an existing project by loading planigin latest script and comments.
expected_behavior: Encoding on restart, user can choose to continue existing project.
Encoding Coder is presented with plan and latest script/comments.
negative_cases: Encoding continuing project fails to load latest files.
Encoding continuing project starts from scratch.

requirements.description: Encoding iteration loop must terminate only when user is satisfied; no automatic termination after fixed number of iterations.
expected_behavior: Encoding loop continues until user terminates program.
Encoding no code to exit program gracefully.
negative_cases: Encoding loop terminates after fixed number of iterations.
Encoding program exits without user action.

semantic_graph_review.semantic_graph_review: The provided profile describes a multi-agent iterative coding system with four agents (manager, planner, programmer, reviewer) and two tools (write_latest_iteration, write_settled_plan). The message edges show the manager initiating chats with the other three agents, which is consistent with the manager's role as the human proxy orchestrating the workflow. The agent-tool links correctly assign the two tools to the manager, as the manager is the only agent that should persist plan and code iterations. The requirements (R1-R8) are well-defined and align with the agent roles and expected behaviors. The raw notes list additional functions from various files, but the core agent/tool/message edge structure appears logically sound. No missing or incorrect edges are identified based on the profile.

suspected_risk_points.evidence: The tools 'write_latest_iteration' and 'write_settled_plan' are listed with empty parameters and no signature or docstring in the profile. The source file is 'IterativeTools.py', but the profile does not provide the actual function signatures. This could lead to AutoGen integration issues if the tool schemas are not properly registered or if the LLM generates incorrect calls due to missing parameter descriptions.

The planner agent is expected to call 'write_settled_plan' according to requirement R1, but the agent-tool links only assign this tool to the manager. The planner's system message instructs it to call 'write_settled_plan', but without the tool being registered to the planner, the call will fail or be ignored by the AutoGen framework.

The message edges only show manager initiating chats with planner, programmer, and reviewer. There are no edges for the planner to communicate back to the manager for approval, or for the reviewer to provide feedback to the programmer. The group chat mechanism (likely from AndyTools.py) may handle speaker selection dynamically, but the static graph lacks these edges, which could indicate a missing or implicit communication path.
